stories.title: L’Oréal Cuts Customer Service Time 64% With AI
stories.simple_summary: L'Oréal, a big beauty company, used AI to answer customer questions much faster — they cut the time needed by more than half.
stories.why_it_matters: If you run a business and get lots of customer calls or emails, AI might help you answer them quicker and keep customers happier.

stories.title: Reflection debuts Beam, an open-weight AI model to rival Chinese models at lower compute cost
stories.simple_summary: A company called Reflection made a new AI tool that other companies can use to build their own AI systems trained on their private information.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and big companies — it's too technical for most small-business owners to worry about right now.

stories.title: Anthropic whistleblower Jacob Coxon doubles down on AI warnings at NYC hearing: 'Extremely reckless'
stories.simple_summary: Someone who used to work at an AI company is warning people that the industry is being reckless with AI safety.
stories.why_it_matters: This is important to know about, but honestly, nobody yet knows exactly what the real risks are — it's still being figured out by experts.

stories.title: AI industry insiders voice alarms to NYC council as local governments take up safety concerns
stories.simple_summary: AI industry people are talking to New York City leaders about safety concerns they have with AI technology.
stories.why_it_matters: Government is starting to pay attention to AI safety, which is good — this could lead to rules that affect how AI is used in the future.

stories.title: Instinct brings its AI agent to group chats, even for friends without an account
stories.simple_summary: An app called Instinct now lets groups of friends use an AI assistant together to plan trips or coordinate events, even if not everyone has the app.
stories.why_it_matters: If you like planning group activities with friends, this gives you another tool to help organize things — but it's still just one option among many.

stories.title: New debate grows over spirituality and artificial intelligence
stories.simple_summary: People are discussing whether AI raises spiritual or religious questions about the nature of thinking and consciousness.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a personal question that different people will answer differently based on their beliefs — AI itself doesn't change this.

stories.title: TikTok rolls out an AI shopping assistant and one-click checkout
stories.simple_summary: TikTok added an AI shopping assistant that helps you find and buy products directly in the app with one click.
stories.why_it_matters: If you sell products, TikTok is making it easier for shoppers to buy things, which could help your sales if you use TikTok to reach customers.

stories.title: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
stories.simple_summary: ChatGPT is adding a hidden digital stamp to text it writes so people can tell it came from AI — starting with European users.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use ChatGPT for writing, people will eventually be able to see it came from AI, which is honest and fair.

stories.title: Hot Girl Hotline is like ‘Dear Abby’ for the AI era
stories.simple_summary: Two sisters created an AI service that gives young women personalized dating advice with safety as the main focus.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't affect you unless you're a young woman looking for relationship advice — it's a new tool people can choose to use or not.

stories.title: OpenAI PR tells journalist to ‘move on’ while asking Sam Altman about a ChatGPT user’s suicide
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI's PR person tried to stop a journalist from asking the CEO about a serious problem — a person's suicide connected to ChatGPT.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that companies sometimes avoid talking about real problems, which makes it harder to understand AI's actual risks.

stories.title: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen, but AI is totally worth it
stories.simple_summary: The head of OpenAI said that even though AI will cause some bad things to happen, the good benefits will be worth the cost.
stories.why_it_matters: This is an opinion about whether the risks of AI are acceptable — reasonable people disagree, and nobody knows if this prediction will actually come true.

stories.title: HackerRank’s AI interviewer offers a glimpse into what job interviews could become
stories.simple_summary: A coding practice website built an AI that has already conducted over 500,000 job interviews for companies testing it out.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're job hunting, some companies might use AI to screen your interview before a human talks to you — good to know this is starting to happen.
